title: Small Warm Light
theme: Buying comfort while hurting, and forgiving yourself for it
hook_line: I bought myself a little light
style: Intimate acoustic folk-pop, hushed and reflective, warm breathy close-mic vocal, fingerpicked nylon guitar, soft upright piano, brushed snare, 78 bpm
exclude: autotune, spoken intro, electronic drums, yelling, orchestral swells, trap hi-hats, heavy bass drop
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Paper bag warm on the seat beside me
Radio low and the lot still wet
Phone screen cracked across the same bad number
I swore I'd wait, then I was pulling in

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the math, I know the hour
I know the sound a bill makes at the door
But my hands were tired and the bag was hot
So I let the small things in before

[Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Verse 2]
Hoodie two sizes too big for grief
Receipts folded small inside my coat
A candle from the drugstore, lit for no one
Whispering the sorry I still owe

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the math, I know the hour
I know the sound a bill makes at the door
But the night was long and the window was black
So I let the warm things in, and I'm back

[Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Bridge]
Who taught us comfort was a crime?
Hurt people reach for what is near
The bag was never the whole story
The shame was heavier than the paper
So ask what the hurt was asking for
And meet it with a kinder hand tomorrow

[Final Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Outro]
Porch light on, the door unlocked
Tomorrow I can start again
A little light, a little rest
I'm allowed to be both the hurt and the healing

video_notes: Open slow on the candle flame and rain on glass, then cut to hands and objects (the bag, the cracked phone face-down, folded receipts) on the verse lines. Let the chorus hold on the candle with a gentle push-in, and end the outro on the flame dimming to a warm glow with no hard cut.
description: A song about the small comforts we reach for when we're hurting, and the harder work of forgiving ourselves for reaching. It's about people trying to get through the night, not a lesson about money.
